q: How do I change the colour of a red car to blue in my shot?
a: 1. Add a node for the change (`grade.addNode`) after your balance node. 2. Qualifier tab: Pick on the car's red (`grade.pickQualifier`), Add a lighter and a darker part of the paint, then set View to Matte: the car white, everything else black. Raise Qualifier softness or Matte blur if the edge chatters. 3. If other red things are caught, add a Circle or Rectangle window around the car on the same node (`masks.add`), tracked if it moves (`masks.track`): the node then acts only where both select. 4. View back to Normal; in Primaries push the hue towards blue (Gain and Gamma wheels towards blue, Saturation as needed). Options: a big hue jump (red to blue) can look painted on reflections; Lumetri's HSL Secondary does the same with its key and correction if you work in Premiere style.

q: make her yellow dress look green
a: Qualify the dress on its own node: Pick the yellow (`grade.pickQualifier`), widen with Add, check the Matte view so skin stays black (narrow Hue width if a face shows grey). Then shift it towards green with the wheels in Primaries. Skin shares warm hues with yellow, so limit the selection with a soft window around her (`masks.add`) and track it (`masks.track`) if she moves. Quicker but rougher: Lumetri's Hue vs Hue curve on the yellow range; narrow curve bumps can tear gradients in compressed footage.

q: Recolour a product for a colourway variant: grey sneaker to navy, without touching the white sole.
a: 1. Separate node, qualifier on the grey upper (`grade.pickQualifier`), Luminance high lowered so the white sole drops out of the matte; check with View ▸ Matte. 2. A tracked window (`masks.add`, `masks.track`) around the shoe keeps the floor and background out. 3. Push Gain and Gamma towards blue and lower Gamma for navy; grey has little saturation, so the qualifier range is narrow: soften the matte rather than widening it. 4. Compare against a still of the real navy product (`stills.grab`) if you have one. A low-saturation colour like grey is the hardest to key; a matte pass in Matte view on several frames catches flicker.

q: I have a static shot of a city skyline, I want it to slowly go from day to night over 10 seconds.
a: Animate a grade over the clip: add Lumetri (`effects.apply`, effect `lumetri`) and keyframe it (every Lumetri slider is an effect parameter, `effects.setParam`, keyframed with the stopwatch): at the start the day values; at the end Exposure down, Temperature cooler, Saturation lower. Ease the keyframes (`effects.setInterpolation`) so the change starts and ends gently. To keep windows and street lights bright as it darkens, the node grader gives you shape control: a node with ellipse windows on the lights (`masks.add`) that stays brighter. A real night plate dissolved over the day plate (Cross Dissolve) is the other option if you filmed both, and looks more real.

q: sun going down effect on a locked off shot, sky gets orange then dark blue
a: Two keyframed stages on Lumetri (`effects.apply`, `lumetri`): first warm it (Temperature up, Highlights a little down) for the sunset, then cool and darken (Temperature down, Exposure down, Saturation down) for dusk; keyframe each slider with the stopwatch and ease them (`effects.setInterpolation`). For the sky alone, a node with a Linear window (`masks.add`) over the sky darkens it most, as in day for night. Hard shadows from a high sun give it away, so this works best on overcast or shaded shots.

q: Can I keyframe the node grader to transition a grade over time, or only Lumetri?
a: Lumetri is the dependable route: every Lumetri slider is an effect parameter that keyframes like any effect (`effects.setParam`, the stopwatch, `effects.setInterpolation`). For a change from one complete node grade to another, cut the clip (`sequence.addEdit`) and put a dissolve between two pieces with different grades, or stack a copy on V2 with the second grade and keyframe its Opacity from 0 to 100 %. Trade-off: the copy route lets you use full node grades (windows, qualifiers) on both ends; Lumetri keyframes are simpler for a steady shift.

q: A short intro where my logo appears with a light leak and a whoosh.
a: 1. The logo as a graphic (or a PNG with transparency) on V2 over black or a background on V1. 2. Animate it in: keyframe Scale from slightly smaller and Opacity from 0 (`effects.setParam`, eased with `effects.setInterpolation`). 3. Light: the Light Leaks effect (Video Effects ▸ Lights & Glows) on the logo or an adjustment layer above, or a light-leak clip on black above it with Opacity Blend Mode Screen. 4. Sound: a whoosh on an SFX track lined up with the move. 5. Save it as a template (`graphics.template.export`) to reuse on every video.

q: logo glows then fades into the first shot
a: Put the logo on V2 above your first shot. Add Wonder Glow (Video Effects ▸ Lights & Glows) and keyframe its Intensity up for the glow; then keyframe the logo's Opacity down to 0 over a second so the shot underneath takes over (`effects.setParam`, ease the keyframes). Alternatively a Cross Dissolve at the end of the logo clip into the shot on V1. Keep the whole intro short: a few seconds before the content.

q: Logo sting I can reuse across a series, with protected in/out animation when I change its length.
a: Build the logo graphic with its in and out moves, then set protected time (`graphics.setResponsiveTime`) so the first and last seconds keep their animation when the clip is trimmed or stretched. Export it as a template (`graphics.template.export`) with nothing or only a subtitle editable; apply it in each episode (`graphics.template.apply`). To share it with someone else, put it in a look pack (`packs.export`).

q: I filmed a music video, the band played along to the track 5 times. How do I line it all up?
a: 1. Put the master song on the timeline as the audio. 2. Sync each take to it by audio: select a take and the song and Synchronize by audio (`clip.synchronize`), or Merge Clips. 3. Make a multicam of the synced takes and cut between them while playing; the song stays the only audio. 4. Check lip sync on a few close-ups and slip a take by frames if needed. Takes where the camera's own sound is poor sync less reliably: a clap at the start of each take helps.

q: lip sync is off by a couple frames on one take
a: Select that take's video and slip it a frame at a time (the nudge / slip keys on the timeline) until the lips match the song, checking on a close-up with hard consonants (p, b, m). If the take was synced by audio, re-run Synchronize (`clip.synchronize`) with the song selected; frame-level drift over a long take usually means a variable-frame-rate recording.

q: Music video: cut wide and close takes on the beat after syncing them.
a: After the takes are synced to the song and in a multicam, drop markers on the beats or phrases while playing (M, `markers.add`), turn on Snap (`sequence.snap`) and cut angles at the markers. Cut on phrases and accents rather than every beat. Grade the angles so wide and close match before the final pass.

q: make my clip look like it's playing on an old CRT television
a: 1. The look: apply the bundled VHS shader effect (Video Effects ▸ User ▸ Stylize, `effects.apply`) for scanlines, colour bleed and soft blacks; lower Saturation a little and lift blacks with the master curve. 2. For a real TV in the room: put the clip on V2 and pin it onto a TV prop with Corner Pin and Track Surface (`tracking.cornerPin`). Shader effects run only on the GPU.

q: Retro TV channel switch between clips, static and a jump.
a: Use the VHS Damage or Glitch transition (Video Transitions ▸ Grunge & Distort) on the edit, a few frames long. For noise between channels, a short static clip on black placed over the cut works too. Add a click or static burst on an SFX track at the same frame.

q: CRT look but the text in my video gets too blurry to read
a: Turn the VHS shader's colour bleed and wobble down, or put the text on its own track above the clip with the effect so titles stay crisp. Real tape is soft, so keep the picture soft and the information sharp. Check the export at full screen.

q: The 'yep, that's me, you're probably wondering how I got here' freeze frame with a record scratch.
a: 1. Insert Frame Hold Segment at the moment (`clip.insertFrameHoldSegment`, 2 s by default). 2. Punch in on the hold: Motion Scale up and Position on your face. 3. A text graphic with the line; optionally drain the colour: an Adjustment Layer (File ▸ New) above the hold with Lumetri, Saturation keyframed down to 0. 4. A record-scratch sound effect on the first frame of the hold and duck or cut the music there.

q: freeze frame with a name tag popping in next to each person
a: Freeze with Frame Hold (`clip.frameHold`) or Insert Frame Hold Segment. Add a graphic per name on a track above, each with a short in animation (Scale and Opacity keyframes, eased with `effects.setInterpolation`). Save one as a template (`graphics.template.export`) with only the text editable to make the rest quickly.

q: Comedic zoom-in on someone's face with a dramatic sound.
a: Cut at the moment and keyframe Motion Scale fast from 100 % to around 150 % over a few frames on the face (Position keeps it centred); Hold interpolation (`effects.setInterpolation`) at the end makes it snap. High-resolution footage keeps the zoom sharp. Put the sting on an SFX track on the same frame.

q: turn the person standing in front of the sunset into a dark silhouette
a: 1. Lower Lift and Gamma on a contrast node so the person goes black while the sky stays bright. 2. Warm the bright sky: Gain towards orange, a soft highlight shoulder. 3. If the sky is clipping, a Linear window (`masks.add`) over it lets you pull it down separately. Exposed for the sky at the shoot, this needs only small moves; a properly exposed face takes heavy crushing that adds noise.

q: Silhouette with the sun flaring and a warm glow around the edge.
a: Crush the person to black with Lift and Gamma down, warm the highlights with the Gain wheel, then add Wonder Glow (Video Effects ▸ Lights & Glows) with a warm Glow Color and a high Threshold so only the sun and the rim bloom. Check the shadows aren't lifted by the glow.

q: silhouette but keep a little detail in the face
a: Pull Lift down less and use a soft ellipse window on the face (`masks.add`, tracked with `masks.track`) with Gamma raised slightly, so the face keeps a hint of detail while the rest stays dark. Too much lift reveals noise in log shadows; a spatial NR node first helps.

q: Workout video with a countdown timer on screen for each exercise.
a: Revolution has no countdown text yet (Metadata & Timecode Burn-in only counts up, from the timecode or frame count). Options: 1. A text graphic per second (a short clip each, '30', '29', …) built from a template so only the number changes (`graphics.template.apply`); quick to place with the clips snapped end to end. 2. Make the countdown once as a clip elsewhere (with transparency) and import it. 3. A progress bar instead: a box shape whose Scale or Position is keyframed across the exercise, simpler and readable at a glance.

q: exercise name and reps in the corner during each set
a: A lower-third style graphic per exercise: the box pinned to the text (`graphics.pin`) so it fits any name, inside the safe margins; saved as a template with the name and reps editable (`graphics.template.export`). Keep it on screen for the whole set and big enough to read on a phone.

q: Interval timer with a beep at the end of each round.
a: No automatic countdown: place a number graphic per second or a keyframed progress bar (a shape layer's Scale over the round). The beep: a short tone clip (the audio of Bars and Tone, trimmed) or a beep sound on an SFX track at each round's end; markers at the round boundaries (`markers.add`) make placing both easy.

q: make a flashback scene feel like a memory
a: A few layers that each say 'memory': 1. Softer, lower-contrast grade with lifted blacks and a little less saturation (or warm and faded). 2. Wonder Glow with a low Threshold for a hazy bloom. 3. Dip to White in and out of the flashback (`sequence.applyVideoTransition` after setting the default with `effects.setDefaultTransition`). 4. Optionally a touch of reverb on the voices (Essential Sound ▸ Creative ▸ Reverb). Keep it consistent so the audience learns the code.

q: Flashback in black and white with grain and a vignette.
a: On the look node: shift colours first (wheels or a qualifier), then Saturation to 0 on a later node; grain on the last node (`grade.param.grain.*`); a soft inverted ellipse window with Gain down for the vignette. Put the look node on every flashback shot (`grade.append`) so it stays identical.

q: dreamy blur around the edges of the frame
a: On a copy of the clip above the original, add Gaussian Blur and draw an ellipse mask on its Opacity (`masks.add`), Inverted and heavily feathered, so only the edges are blurred. Combine with a soft glow for a dream look.

q: Haul video: show the price and name of each item as I hold it up.
a: A lower-third template with item name and price editable (`graphics.template.apply`, change the fields in Essential Graphics ▸ Edit), placed when each item appears. If you move the item around, a small price tag graphic can follow it with Attach to Track on its Motion (`tracking.attach`, Position only). Keep text big and inside the safe area for phones.

q: zoom on the label of the product when I talk about it
a: Cut at that moment and punch in: Motion Scale up and Position on the label (high-resolution footage keeps it sharp), or keyframe a slow push with eased keyframes. A highlight box shape around the label in a graphic adds emphasis.

q: Item-by-item chapters so viewers can skip to each product.
a: Put a marker at the start of each item named after it (`markers.addChapter` or `markers.add`), export them with Export Markers as CSV (`markers.exportCsv`) and paste the times into the description, the first at 0:00. YouTube ignores chapters under ten seconds.
